     1	import dlt
     2	from pyspark.sql.functions import col, trim, regexp_replace, when, length, to_date
     3	from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
     4	
     5	spark = SparkSession.getActiveSession()
     6	catalog = spark.conf.get("catalog")
     7	target_schema = spark.conf.get("target_schema")  # silver target schema, e.g., consumer_silver
     8	# Derive bronze schema from silver target
     9	bronze_schema = target_schema.replace("_silver", "_bronze")
    10	bronze_table = f"{catalog}.{bronze_schema}.consumer_mv"
    11	
    12	@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_consumer_id", "consumer_id IS NOT NULL")
    13	@dlt.table(
    14	    name="consumer_mv",
    15	    comment="Silver consumer view with cleaned data",
    16	    table_properties={"quality": "silver"},
    17	    schema="""
    18	        consumer_id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    19	        name STRING,
    20	        age INT,
    21	        gender STRING,
    22	        email STRING,
    23	        phone STRING,
    24	        address STRING,
    25	        city STRING,
    26	        state STRING,
    27	        country STRING,
    28	        registration_date DATE,
    29	        is_active BOOLEAN
    30	    """
    31	)
    32	def consumer_mv():
    33	    # Read from bronze table as a batch source
    34	    df = spark.read.table(bronze_table)
    35	    # Trim whitespace from string columns
    36	    string_cols = ["name", "gender", "email", "phone", "address", "city", "state", "country"]
    37	    for c in string_cols:
    38	        df = df.withColumn(c, trim(col(c)))
    39	    # Phone: keep digits only
    40	    df = df.withColumn("phone", regexp_replace(col("phone"), r"\D", ""))
    41	    # Nullify phone if less than 10 digits
    42	    df = df.withColumn("phone", when(length(col("phone")) < 10, None).otherwise(col("phone")))
    43	    # Convert registration_date to date type
    44	    df = df.withColumn("registration_date", to_date(col("registration_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))
    45	    return df
